data.answer: TagZ Foods, a Bengaluru-based food tech startup founded in 2019, has experienced significant growth in the Indian snacks market, particularly targeting urban GenZ consumers with innovative, healthier snack options. The company has grown its revenue from Rs 10.34 lakh in FY20 to Rs 23 crore in May 2023, a 230-fold increase over four years. Despite challenges in scaling production and distribution, TagZ Foods has expanded its product portfolio and achieved cash profitability by March 2022. The company was acquired by Reliance Retail Limited in November 2024 for approximately INR 280 mn, aiming to leverage Reliance's retail network to reach 30-40M premium households and pursue global exports. TagZ Foods' revenue streams are driven by direct-to-consumer sales and partnerships with retailers, with reported revenue of INR 734.4 lakh in 2022.

Though apparently small, the numbers look impressive if one views them in the context of where the brand was when it started. Let’s start with the revenue bit. It has jumped from Rs10.34 lakh in FY20 (and this was a truncated fiscal year as the brand was rolled out in February) to Rs1.47 crore the next fiscal and then Rs8.97 crore in FY22. Overall, in four years, the brand has grown by 230 times. TagZ Foods is a modern snack brand specializing in healthier, air-popped potato chips, catering to health-conscious consumers in India. The company, founded in 2019, aims to disrupt the traditional snack industry with its unique product offerings and has gained investment through Shark Tank India. With a strong growth trajectory and plans for international expansion, TagZ Foods is positioned to become a key player in the healthy snacking market.

The company is best known for its “popped” potato chips, which are neither fried nor baked, offering 50% less fat and no cholesterol or trans fats. The company’s operating revenue, however, declined sharply by 90% to Rs 1.3 crore in FY25, down from Rs 14.14 crore in FY24. Meanwhile, other income surged 5.3X to Rs 25.3 crore in FY25 from Rs 4.7 crore in FY24. This spike was primarily driven by gains from the sale of intangible assets during the year, which contributed Rs 23.5 crore. Over time, TagZ has expanded beyond its flagship popped chips into a broader portfolio that includes gourmet dips, cookies, and premium bar snacks. Prior to this, TagZ had raised $1.2 million in seed funding in 2020 from a group of angel investors.
